Finish Block 2; review progress and recovery.

Begin Block 3. Keep unchanged lifts at 100% of Week 21 working weights; new exercises start 10–15% lighter and track separately.
Finish Block 3; review progress and recovery.

reference.text: Stay at the same load until every working set reaches the top of its rep range. Then add the smallest available increment (about 2.5 kg / 5 lb or one cable step) and return toward the bottom of the range.
In Week 1, pick a load that puts the first working set inside the rep range at the target RIR. Adjust during the first session or two.

Compounds stop 1–2 reps short of failure; other isolations are usually 0–1 RIR, with a final safe machine/cable set at failure. Exception: Monday rear-delt fly and Friday lateral raise use normal working loads at strict 1 RIR on every set, with no failure set (use the listed replacement in other blocks).

Weeks 11, 22, 33, and 44: keep the same exercises, cut sets roughly in half, reduce load 10–20%, and stay at 3–4+ RIR. No failure or PRs. After the deload, unchanged exercises resume at 100% of their pre-deload working weight; use a 2.5–5% buffer for that session only if needed.

Switch blocks only after deloads. Unchanged lifts resume at 100% of pre-deload working weight; if target RIR is out of reach, reduce 2.5–5% for that session only. Only new/swapped exercises start 10–15% lighter, then rebuild via double progression. Keep the four main lifts consistent.
About 5 minutes easy cardio. Before the first exercise: 2–3 ramp-up sets around 50%, 70%, and 85% of working load for 5, 3, and 1 reps. One light set before each other exercise.
Use a controlled 1–2 second lowering phase, full stretch, no bouncing, and full range of motion.
Monday Upper A; Tuesday Lower A; Wednesday Push B; Thursday Pull B; Friday Lower B; weekends off. Target session length about 60–75 minutes. Log every working set.
About +200–300 kcal/day above maintenance; protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day; fat at least 0.6–0.8 g/kg/day; aim for about 0.25–0.5% bodyweight gain per week. Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day.
Sleep 7–9 hours; 7,000–10,000 steps/day. Track weekly bodyweight averages and note recovery/pain.

Target about 300–500 kcal/day below maintenance, protein 2.2–2.6 g/kg/day, and about 0.5–1% bodyweight loss/week. Consider deloads every 5–6 weeks or earlier if needed.
Between a deficit and surplus, use 1–2 weeks at maintenance; lean toward 2–4 weeks if the cut lasted 12 weeks or more.
Deload early if performance drops for 2+ weeks, joints ache persistently, sleep quality tanks, or motivation collapses. Swap a painful movement pattern; do not train through sharp pain.

If a lift has stalled 3–4 weeks, review sleep and food before changing the exercise. If a session is missed, skip it and carry on—do not double up. After a missed week or more, repeat the last completed week 5–10% lighter.
Use the nearest same-row option when equipment is unavailable. The program lists alternatives for shoulder press, rear delts, split squats/lunges, and some machine/cable movements.

Use lifting straps on Thursday shrugs and Friday barbell RDLs. On Thursday rows and pulldowns, use straps whenever grip gives out before your back does, so grip does not limit posterior-chain training.
